plain_english_policy: This bill establishes a legal shield for private hospitals (including denominational ones), their employees, and physicians in Alabama against being forced to participate in specific medical procedures they object to on ethical or religious grounds. Specifically, it prohibits requiring these entities to use facilities for abortions, stem cell research, cloning, euthanasia, or physician-assisted suicide. It also forbids hospitals from disciplining staff based on their beliefs regarding these acts and bars conditioning employment benefits (like pay or promotion) on agreeing to perform them.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would create a statutory right for healthcare providers in Alabama to refuse participation in abortions, stem cell research, cloning, euthanasia, or physician-assisted suicide without fear of losing their jobs, facing discipline, or being sued. It effectively mandates that private hospitals cannot force staff to perform these procedures and protects the employment status of those who object on moral grounds.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors affirmatively advanced a bill protecting religiously or ethically motivated healthcare providers from being compelled to perform abortions and other contested procedures.
evidence_quotes: "No private or denominational hospital shall be required to permit its facilities to be utilized for the performance of abortions, dispensation of abortifacient drugs, human embryonic stem cell research..."
"No physician or employee ... shall be required to perform or to assist or participate in an abortion ... if that individual objects to such acts on ethical, moral, or religious grounds."
"A civil action for damages or reinstatement of employment, or both, may be brought for any violation of the provisions of this act."
